rescoredNote: Re-measured after the asserted-field scoring-fairness fix (category/payee scored only when the label is non-null) — unchanged from the initial seed: same overall accuracy and same passing-case ids, since the labels were traced from the heuristic's own output.
rescoredNote2: 2026-09-30 — denominator reconciliation (evals/score.mjs's aggregate()): overallAccuracy is now scored over ALL 39 cases (parse cases + refusal/fail-to-parse cases, a refusal case counted correct on a null return), matching the population the --n-repeat pass-rate gate always used, instead of the 32 parse-cases-only denominator. 21/32 correct parse cases + 7/7 correctly-refused cases = 28/39 = 0.7179... — NOT a real accuracy change: parseAccuracy (21/32 = 0.65625, unchanged) is the old overallAccuracy verbatim; passingCaseIds and every underlying case result are identical to the prior baseline.
reseededNote: Step 1b.1 — dataset grown from 39 to 150 hand-labelled cases (111 new, spread across income/refund/transfer/sign, amount formats, dates, category/payee, terse/noisy, and 10 more fail-to-parse cases) and a committed dev/holdout split added (evals/split.mjs). This baseline is reseeded against the FULL 150-case dataset (default --split=all, matching the default npm run eval invocation with no --split flag) — overallAccuracy therefore drops relative to the old 39-case baseline (0.7179 -> 0.4867); that drop is the NEW cases being harder (many deliberately probe known heuristic gaps — synonym categories, word-number amounts, verbs outside the heuristic's income/transfer regexes, date text the heuristic never reads at all since localParse always returns occurredAt: now), not a regression in the heuristic itself. See evals/README.md's re-baseline section.
